entries.definition: the overall condition of being physically and mentally well
entries.example: The program considers well-being as more than the absence of illness.

entries.definition: the ability to adapt or recover when facing difficulty
entries.example: Supportive relationships can help people build resilience during change.

entries.definition: lasting for a long time or repeatedly returning
entries.example: A person with chronic pain may need an ongoing care plan.

entries.definition: developing suddenly or needing attention over a short period
entries.example: The nurse asked whether the pain was acute or long-lasting.

entries.definition: the identification of a health condition through assessment
entries.example: A diagnosis requires more than matching one symptom to an online list.

entries.definition: a professional judgment about the likely course of an illness
entries.example: The doctor explained that the prognosis depended on several factors.

entries.definition: care and training intended to restore function after illness or injury
entries.example: Her rehabilitation included gradually practicing everyday movements.

entries.definition: treatment intended to improve a health condition
entries.example: The clinician explained the purpose and limits of the recommended therapy.

entries.definition: action intended to stop a problem or illness from occurring
entries.example: The workshop focused on prevention rather than waiting for accidents.

entries.definition: the body’s capacity to defend against a particular infection
entries.example: The lesson explains why immunity is not simply an all-or-nothing condition.

entries.definition: able to pass from one person to another
entries.example: The clinic provided advice about the contagious illness.

entries.definition: caused by or capable of causing infection
entries.example: Not every infectious disease passes directly between people.

entries.definition: the passing of a disease-causing agent between sources or hosts
entries.example: Understanding transmission helps professionals choose suitable precautions.

entries.definition: an organism or agent that can cause disease
entries.example: The laboratory looked for a particular pathogen in the sample.

entries.definition: the body’s response to injury or irritation that can cause swelling or pain
entries.example: The doctor examined the joint for signs of inflammation.

entries.definition: a harmful lack of something the body needs
entries.example: The clinician investigated whether a nutrient deficiency was involved.

entries.definition: a substance the body uses for growth, repair, or energy
entries.example: The table explains the role of each nutrient without promising a cure.

entries.definition: a nutrient used in building and maintaining body tissues
entries.example: Beans are one food that can contribute protein to a meal.

entries.definition: a nutrient group that includes sugars and starches
entries.example: The lesson compares different foods containing carbohydrate.

entries.definition: parts of plant foods that are not fully digested
entries.example: Whole grains and many vegetables provide fiber.

entries.definition: an organic substance needed in small amounts for normal body function
entries.example: The label lists the amount of each vitamin in the supplement.

entries.definition: an inorganic nutrient needed for body functions
entries.example: Iron is a mineral with important roles in the body.

entries.definition: the chemical processes that maintain life in the body
entries.example: The article describes metabolism as many connected processes.

entries.definition: the state or process of having adequate water in the body
entries.example: The coach discussed hydration alongside rest and appropriate training.

entries.definition: tiredness that can affect physical or mental activity
entries.example: Persistent fatigue is a reason to seek appropriate health advice.

entries.definition: a state of extreme tiredness
entries.example: She recognized exhaustion and stopped working for the evening.

entries.definition: work-related exhaustion and detachment linked with prolonged stress
entries.example: The team discussed workload rather than treating burnout as personal weakness.

entries.definition: a strong feeling of worry or unease about possible threats
entries.example: The unfamiliar situation caused anxiety before the interview.

entries.definition: a mental health condition involving persistent low mood or loss of interest
entries.example: Depression can require professional support rather than simple encouragement alone.

entries.definition: knowledge or recognition of a situation or need
entries.example: The campaign increased awareness of available local support.

entries.definition: paying deliberate attention to present experience
entries.example: She used mindfulness to notice distractions without immediately following them.

entries.definition: involving long periods of sitting with little movement
entries.example: His sedentary work encouraged him to plan short movement breaks.

entries.definition: not extreme in amount or intensity
entries.example: The class compared moderate activity with more demanding exercise.

entries.definition: involving strong effort or energetic movement
entries.example: Vigorous exercise requires attention to individual ability and appropriate guidance.

entries.definition: the ability to continue an effort over time
entries.example: The walking group increased endurance gradually rather than rushing.

entries.definition: the ability of joints and muscles to move through a range
entries.example: The trainer checked flexibility before suggesting a suitable stretch.

entries.definition: the ability to move around or move part of the body
entries.example: The building changes improved mobility for people using walking aids.

entries.definition: the position in which someone holds the body
entries.example: Adjusting the screen helped her find a more comfortable posture.

entries.definition: the ability to make body movements work together smoothly
entries.example: The game practices coordination without comparing players’ speed.

entries.definition: the amount of something a person can handle without unacceptable effects
entries.example: Exercise tolerance can differ between people and change over time.

entries.definition: reliance on a substance or support to function
entries.example: The doctor discussed dependence when explaining the medicine’s risks.

entries.definition: the administration of a vaccine to help the immune system recognize a disease
entries.example: The clinic provided information about vaccination and answered questions.

entries.definition: harmful or unfavorable
entries.example: Report an adverse reaction to a qualified health professional.

entries.definition: an effect of a treatment other than its intended main effect
entries.example: The leaflet explains which side effect may require medical advice.

entries.definition: checking people for signs of a condition before clear symptoms appear
entries.example: The invitation explains the purpose and limitations of screening.

entries.definition: a qualified professional providing a particular kind of care
entries.example: The practitioner asked about her history before suggesting next steps.

entries.definition: a professional with advanced knowledge of a particular field
entries.example: The family doctor referred him to a specialist.

entries.definition: an arrangement directing someone to another professional or service
entries.example: The referral included a summary of the earlier examination.

entries.definition: a meeting to seek professional advice
entries.example: She wrote her questions before the medical consultation.

entries.definition: practices that help keep people and surroundings clean
entries.example: Good hygiene includes cleaning shared equipment appropriately.
